results.title: Kodak’s new SlideTag is a keychain tracker with a built-in E Ink photo display | DPReview
results.content:
The SlideTag comes from Reto, the Kodak brand licensee behind the viral Kodak Charmera and other retro-looking Kodak-branded products. Like those products, the SlideTag leans into the current nostalgia for old-school camera gear, and it’s styled to look like a 1935 Kodachrome slide mount.

Like the Charmera, the SlideTag is designed as a collectible. It comes in eight frame designs and is sold in blind boxes, so you don’t know which one you’ll get. Reto also made a rarer “secret edition” with a metallic finish, which has a 1-in-64 chance of turning up. You can buy the whole set, which still gives you a chance at the secret edition.

Kodak Slidetag keychain set featuring a branded product display box, two slide-shaped tags, a film strip, and a marketing brochure.Reto [...] On the tracker side, the SlideTag works with both Apple Find My and Google Find Hub, and it has a 75 dB buzzer to help you find it. It supports Bluetooth 5.4, has a real-time tracking range of up to 30 meters (98 feet) and has an IP54 rating for some protection from the elements. It runs on a replaceable lithium coin cell battery.

You’ll need the free Kodak Memory Link app to upload images to the tracker. The display isn’t limited to photos, and it can also show to-do lists, countdowns, QR codes, contact details and more. A calendar function lets you schedule what to display in advance, and you can create a slideshow loop of up to 12 images.

The Kodak SlideTag is available now for $35 for a single box or $280 for the whole set.

results.title: Kodak SlideTag Electronic Photo Frame Location Tracker Keychain Debuts: Recreating the Classic Film Slide Design - POPBEE
results.content:
# Hanging Film Slides on Your Bag? Kodak's New SlideTag Comes with Built-In Location Tracking

## Even portable location trackers are getting the vintage treatment~

## Summary

- Faithfully recreates the classic 1935 Kodachrome slide frame design, weighing just 16.6 grams to easily clip onto keys or bags.
- Features a 1.54-inch 6-color E-ink screen that can cycle through up to 12 photos offline, or switch to display to-do lists and QR codes.
- Supports both Apple Find My and Google Find Hub location networks, serving as an item tracker and luggage tag.
- Released as a collectible blind box with 8 vintage designs and 1 secret edition. [...] The small accessories clipped to bags or keys can offer more than just cute looks—they can be practical, too. Kodak recently introduced an electronic photo frame and tracker key fob called SlideTag. At first glance, it looks like a tiny vintage film slide, but the image inside changes to match your mood, all while housing built-in location tracking to prevent lost items.

The accessory draws inspiration from the classic Kodachrome color reversal paper slide mounts introduced by Kodak in 1935. SlideTag scales that familiar square paper frame down to a portable size, measuring just 39.3 × 46 × 7.58 mm and weighing around 16.6 g, making it lightweight enough to attach to keyrings, backpacks, or luggage handles without feeling bulky. [...] ### More than a mini electronic photo frame, it also doubles as a portable everyday tool

The front of SlideTag features a 1.54-inch 6-color E-ink screen, which official specs note delivers rich, detailed photo colors. Simply pair it via Bluetooth using the dedicated KODAK Memory Link App to upload shots from your phone’s photo library or snap a picture on the spot. The built-in storage holds up to 12 photos; once set to slideshow mode, the display automatically cycles through the images offline even when disconnected from your phone.

results.title: Kodak aims for Charmera-style hit with adorable SlideTag, a tiny digital photo frame that doubles up as an AirTag | Amateur Photographer
results.content:
The SlideTag is leaning very heavily on nostalgia for Kodak Kodachrome, the iconic 35mm slide film first introduced in 1935. As well as its slide mount presentation, the SlideTag also comes in eight vintage-style designs, several of which are named after Kodachrome. And just like the Charmeras, these designs come in ‘blind’ boxes, meaning you won’t know which one you’ve bought until you open up the box. 

All Kodak SlideTag variant colours

Several of the designs are named after Kodachrome, with the logo prominently featured on the frame, but that seems to be as far as the collaboration goes – there aren’t Kodachrome-style filters placed on your photos or anything like that. [...] Kodak licensee Reto Project has scored a fair few hits with Kodak-branded products – most famously the Charmera, a tiny keychain camera the size of a lipstick. Now, the company is hoping to score big once again with its new Kodak SlideTag.

The SlideTag is several things in one, but at its core it’s a keychain-sized photo frame, visually styled after a 35mm slide mount, bearing a 6-color E-Ink display that can be used to show up to 12 images in a slideshow rotation. These images can be selected and uploaded via the Kodak Memory Link app, available for iOS and Android. The screen carries a resolution of 240 x 240 pixels, and measures 1.54 inches.

Kodak SlideTag held in hand beside a transparency slide [...] Still, the Kodak SlideTag hits a lot of the same cuteness and nostalgia notes as the Charmera, and I wouldn’t be surprised if it attracts a lot of interest from a similar crowd. This is also reflected in the price – like the Charmera, the Kodak SlideTag is extremely affordable, with a retail price of $34.99 (£35) for a single blind box. Or, if you don’t want to leave things to chance, you can buy a set of all eight designs for a total of $279.92 (£280).

results.title: Kodak SlideTag Is a $35 Blind-Box E Ink Photo Display and AirTag Alternative | PetaPixel
results.content:
Reto, the company behind the wildly successful Kodak Charmera, has announced its next blind box-style product: the Kodak SlideTag. It’s a small, color E Ink display with AirTag-like capability and a user-replaceable battery.

The SlideTag uses that E Ink display to allow users to upload their own photos into it and display them like single slides from the golden age of film.

“When Kodak introduced Kodachrome in 1935, the slide mount quickly became the classic way people projected and shared their favorite memories. Families gathered around glowing projectors, watching their favorite moments illuminated inside a simple cardboard frame,” Reto says. [...] “Decades later, the Kodak SlideTag breathes new life into that iconic retro slide frame, bringing a vintage touch to the digital age. Designed as a miniature memory holder, it allows you to digitize your precious moments and easily carry your stories wherever you go.”

The SlideTag measures 39.3(W) x 46(H) x 7.58(D) mm and weighs just 16.6 grams. The central display is 1.54 inches across with a resolution of 240 x 240 pixels. The color E Ink can display up to six colors and because E Ink doesn’t require any power to retain the image, the SlideTag can display a photo and retain other functionality for extended lengths of time without dying.

results.title: Kodak SlideTag: price, specs, and tracking
results.content:
Nine designs are available that all recreate the cardboard-and-plastic slide mounts that Kodachrome made familiar from 1935 onward and that were stored in shoeboxes under beds everywhere. They are built around a 1.54-inch, 6-color E Ink display at 240 x 240 pixels. Photos are loaded through the KODAK Memory Link app, which also handles slideshows, QR codes, and to-do lists.

The tracking works with Apple Find My and Google Find Hub with an approximate range of up to 30 m (98 ft) in open air, and the tag can sound off at 75 dB to help you find it and whatever essential equipment it's attached to. [...] There are 8 standard tags and one 'secret' design, that's probably not so secret anymore

Reto's Kodak SlideTag is a work of slight genius and combines a $34.99 keychain with an E Ink photo screen and Apple and Google device tracking.

Just in time for Christmas, Kodak licensee Reto, the company behind the zeitgeist-friendly hit Charmera camera, has launched the Kodak SlideTag, a clever little device that mashes together three things and thus becomes an impressive small object of desire.

It is a keychain with an AirTag-like Bluetooth tracker, it is a customizable E Ink display that will display your own photos, and it is a heady nostalgic trip for anyone who remembers the mingled joy and horror of family slide shows. It is a fourth thing as well, a blind box, but nothing's perfect. [...] It is small and light at 39.3 x 46 x 7.58 mm (1.55 x 1.81 x 0.30 in) and 16.6 g (0.6 oz), and has an IP54 rating so it will handle splashes and dust but is not waterproof. It runs on a replaceable CR2032 coin cell.

## Pricing and availability

Like the Charmera, the SlideTag is sold as a blind box, at $34.99. There are eight standard designs plus one secret edition with a 1/64 chance, while a whole set of eight is currently $210. Reto says that one of the basic editions will be replaced if the secret edition appears in the set.
